title: Windows hotkeys conflict with Powertoys's, even after changing the latter

status.label: Needs focused investigation
status.detail: PowerToys shortcuts reportedly fail even after reassignment; Win+Space also invokes the Windows keyboard-layout switcher.

proposed_fixes.title: Make remapped module hotkeys reliably register
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: one reassigned non-conflicting hotkey is not registered or dispatched; a Windows-reserved default is a separate possible conflict.
plan: Obtain and reproduce one exact non-conflicting hotkey and module configuration.
Trace registration and dispatch for that module, including any registration failure.
Fix the verified registration or dispatch defect and test both normal and conflicting shortcuts.
verification: An available configured hotkey activates its module and conflicts are not mistaken for successful registration.

reproduce.title: Make remapped module hotkeys reliably register
prerequisites: Windows and an enabled PowerToys module
setup: Choose a hotkey that is not used by Windows or another app.
steps: Assign that shortcut to one reported module.
Restart PowerToys and press the shortcut in a supported context.
Record the exact keys and compare with the default Windows-reserved shortcut.
reproduce.expected_result: The non-conflicting configured shortcut activates the selected module.

comment.body: Thanks for the attached report and for checking multiple PowerToys shortcuts. Win+Space is also used by Windows, so it does not explain the separate remapping issue. Could you share one affected module and the exact non-conflicting shortcut you assigned, and describe what happens after saving and pressing it?
